claim: An application from a person from a safe country of origin goes into the accelerated procedure and can be rejected as manifestly unfounded if the person has not shown serious reasons why the country is not safe for them.

claim: The Questura must tell an applicant from a safe country of origin, when the application is lodged, that it may be rejected.
quote: The Questura shall inform the applicant, at the moment of lodging of the application that if they come from a designated country of safe origin, their application may be rejected.

claim: On 23 February 2026 the Council of the EU formally adopted the first EU-wide list of safe countries of origin.

claim: The EU list designates Bangladesh, Colombia, Egypt, India, Kosovo, Morocco and Tunisia as safe countries of origin at EU level.

claim: The EU safe-country list applies from 12 June 2026, with the rest of the Pact on Migration and Asylum.
quote: will begin to apply on 12 June 2026, at the same time as the rest of the migration and asylum pact.

claim: Member states can keep their own national lists of safe countries alongside the EU list.
quote: Member states will still be able to have their own national lists with additional third countries, which they consider as safe.

claim: The European Commission can suspend a country, or part of its territory or population, from the EU safe list after a substantiated assessment.
quote: An entire country, or part of its territory or population, may be suspended by the European Commission from being designated as safe at the EU level, following a substantiated assessment.

claim: Under the EU Asylum Procedure Regulation, an application is examined in the accelerated procedure if the applicant's nationality has an EU-wide recognition rate of 20% or lower in the latest yearly Eurostat data, unless the person belongs to a category for whom that rate is not representative.
quote: for which the proportion of decisions by the determining authority granting international protection is, according to the latest available yearly Union-wide average Eurostat data, 20 % or lower

claim: The accelerated examination must end no later than three months after the application is lodged.
quote: The determining authority shall conclude the accelerated examination procedure as soon as possible and no later than three months from the date on which the application is lodged.

claim: Under Italy's implementing decree the border procedure is compulsory for people from countries with an acceptance rate below 20%, people who are a danger to national security, and people who gave false information or documents.
quote: The border procedure, in implementation of the provisions of the new Pact, will be compulsory in the case of individuals who are dangerous to national security, who come from countries with an acceptance rate of less than 20%; who have submitted false information or documents.

claim: Italy must examine up to 16,032 applications a year in the border procedure between 12 June 2026 and 12 June 2027.
quote: will have to examine up to 16,032 applications per year in the first period of application between 12 June 2026 and 12 June 2027

claim: During the border procedure the applicant must stay at or near the border or in another designated place, which does not count as entry into Italy.

claim: People in prison or a pre-removal centre also have the right to apply for asylum.
quote: Even if you are in a prison or being held in a pre-removal facility, you have the right to apply for international protection.

claim: At registration the police record personal details and reasons, take a photo and fingerprints (stored in Eurodac), and may ask for the passport.
quote: If you have a passport, you might be requested to hand it over to the Police.

claim: The applicant may hand in a written account of their story, in Italian or another language.
quote: you can also submit a written document (in Italian or another language) in which you explain your story and the reasons for your application.

claim: Interpreting at registration is free.
quote: you have the right to be assisted by an interpreter for free.

claim: Asylum information is confidential and is not shared with the authorities of the country of origin without consent.
quote: will not share any information –without your consent–with any external persons, including authorities of your country of origin.

claim: No lawyer is needed to apply; a lawyer before the Commission is at the applicant's own expense; reception centres and NGOs give free legal support.
quote: many NGOs and associations can also provide you with free legal support.

quote: If your application has been rejected, you can lodge your appeal against this decision. In this case, you need to be assisted by a lawyer.

quote: accedere al patrocinio a spese dello Stato.
